where: iVUE → Cat Item / C&C Code field on the agreement. The 7-char provisioning code that sets the actual speed profile.
note: Distinct from the speed-tier ID (D000). Maps 1:1 to a speed tier + monthly cost. Some are restricted by facility group.

where: iVUE → the monthly recurring cost tied to a C&C code.
note: Cost tiers track the speed bucket. Beasore and development-code tiers price differently.

where: C&C provisioning rule → which speed codes can coexist on one agreement.
example: Can have 1 of each group; only 1 of these per group
note: Governs which tiers are mutually exclusive vs combinable when provisioning. From the C&C reference table.

where: iVUE → Internal Serv Type column. The speed-bucket classification of the agreement.
note: Buckets agreements by speed band; pairs with C&C code. iVUE export col: Internal Serv Type.

where: C&C reference → special location/development service codes (L000/L001/L002...).
note: Development-specific tiers for FTTH subdivisions: Mira Bella/MRBL, Bella Vista/RNSE-Renaissance, Tesoro Viejo/TSVJ. Tie to GIS Sites folders.

where: C&C reference → Beasore-only speed codes (special remote area).
note: Beasore Meadows area has its own restricted tier set (BB Beasore Max). Seen on Beasore orders flagged *REFER TO ENGINEERING*.

where: iVUE → SO → Office Information tab → Complete By Date field. This IS the DUE DATE referenced in requests.
note: Confirmed on the iVUE SO Office Information tab. Paired with Complete By Time. 'DUE DATE' in the request text = this field.

where: iVUE → SO → Office Information tab → Complete By Time field.
note: Companion to Complete By Date.

where: iVUE → SO record → the row of tabs on the service order.
example: SO | Workflow | Agmt | General | Interfaces | Toll | Dir | Local | Serv Addr | 911 | Tax | Equip | Deposit | P&S
note: The full tab set on an iVUE service order. Workflow tab holds the task chain; Serv Addr holds the service point; Equip holds equipment.

where: iVUE → SO grid → SO Type column.
note: Order classification (CONN, DISC, etc). iVUE export/grid col: SO Type.

where: iVUE → SO grid → SO Status column.
note: Lifecycle state of the order. iVUE grid col: SO Status.

where: iVUE → SO grid → Hold SO flag / Office Information → Hold SO checkbox.
note: Marks an order on hold (e.g. Beasore order put in hold pending engineering).

where: iVUE → SO → Workflow tab → task seq 19.0. The Engineering Facilities task — the GIS/facility-assignment step.
note: THIS IS CODY'S TASK in the SO workflow chain. Status QUEUE until worked, then COMP. Appears as alert E.FACS(1). Complete via right-click → Complete or Continue Workflow.

where: iVUE → Workflow tab → task seq 20.0. Programming — switch provisioning step after E.FACS.
note: Next task after E.FACS. Some orders route here (P:PROG) after facilities.

where: iVUE → SO → Workflow tab → ordered task list (Task / Task Seq / Critical / Priority / Needed / Current Status).
note: The full 27-task SO lifecycle. Prefixes: C=Customer Service, N=NOC/Network Ops, I=Internet Dept, E=Engineering(GIS), P=Programming/Provisioning. E.FACS (19) is GIS. Each task has a sequence number and status (COMP/QUEUE).

where: iVUE → SO action bar → Continue Workflow button. Advances the SO to the next task after completing E.FACS.
note: How you hand the SO off after finishing facilities. Also Review SO, Validate/Close, Void, Print, Create SO on the same bar.

where: LinePacks → _LinePacks1 table → the exact column headers.
example: Switch | Equipment | Status | Voice Agreement | Data Agreement | Line/BP | Card Type
note: Confirmed from the _LinePacks1 Access table. Switch=CSX, Equipment=node/card/port, Line/BP=binding post. Search via Ctrl+F in the relevant column.

where: LinePacks → _LinePacks1 → Voice Agreement column. The phone agreement tied to a port.
note: Pairs the physical port to the voice (TEL) agreement. iVUE side = Agreement.

where: LinePacks → _LinePacks1 → Data Agreement column. The internet agreement tied to a port.
note: Pairs the physical port to the data (DSL/internet) agreement. iVUE side = Account.

where: LinePacks → _LinePacks1 → Card Type column (last column). The manufacturer/model of the card the port lives on.
note: Determines bonding compatibility — both bonded legs must share card type. Adtran vs Calix rules apply.

where: Splitter turn-up response → FEEDER section. The backbone leg from GPON cabinet to the FDP.
note: Top section of a splitter turn-up. Cabinet GPON port to Fiber Distribution Point. BNDL = the cabinet/site prefix.

where: Splitter turn-up response → the FDP cross-connect (FDP-IN >> FDP-OUT).
note: Middle leg: the FDP cross-connect mapping in to out. BNDX = cross-connect point.

where: Splitter turn-up response → DISTRIBUTION section. Splitter port out to the MST port at the pedestal.
note: Bottom leg: splitter port to distribution cable/pair to MST port + AH pedestal. (3X5) = splitter ratio context.

where: Fiber Distribution Point — the cross-connect housing between feeder and distribution fiber.
note: Where feeder fiber cross-connects to distribution. Has IN and OUT pair positions.

where: The GPON cabinet/site prefix in fiber strings (e.g. BNDL = Bandit/site cabinet).
note: Site-cabinet identifier prefixing GPON and splitter strings. Pairs with a wire-center splitter (e.g. CKSD).

where: The procedure + response for bringing a new fiber splitter into service (new FTTH area).
example: Corning Dual 1X16 splitter, SFP 100-05148, UPCSC/SC SM DX 2M
note: Documents equipment installed (splitter, SFP, jumpers) plus the full FEEDER/X-CONNECT/DISTRIBUTION fiber path. Picked up from warehouse, logged in note.

where: \\ptc27\Drawings\DataPortal\LinkedDocs\GIS\Sites\ — per-site folder index mapping wire center → site name → exchange.
note: Maps codes to FTTH developments: TSVJ=Tesoro Viejo, MRBL=Mira Bella, PRSV=Friant Preserve, RNSE=Renaissance, CRES/LCRS=Cressman, SNRK=Sunrock, WLDF=Wildflower, DTON=Downtown O'Neals, etc. Also holds PTC FiberBook.xlsx, FRNT CLX ONT CRV Pool.txt, Calix_MGCP_PON_Construction.png.

where: iVUE → Query Builder → Category=Service Points, View='Service Point - Facilities with Serv Addr Status'. Filter to find subscribers/facilities.
note: How to pull all service points on a cable or in an area. Configure Columns / Load / Save / View SQL / Max Rows. Returns Serv Address City, Service Address, Tax Zone, Wire Center, SP Description, SP Remarks.

where: iVUE → Query Builder / Service Point result → Tax Zone column.
note: Tax jurisdiction for the service point. Appears in subscriber query results.

where: iVUE → Service Point → Wire Center column. The serving wire-center code.
note: 4-letter wire-center/CLLI code identifying the serving office. Drives equipment lookup.

where: NewNet CMS → SQL view [NewNetCMS].[dbo].[IVUE_CablePair_Facs_Copper]. The copper cable/pair/facility join used for cutsheets.
note: 47-column view joining cable pair to facility/cross-connect/binding-post. Cols include XConn Cable Nm, MinSvPt_BP, Port_BP, bnd_pair, xconpair, CBOL, Cat Item, SubDown/SubUp. Used to build cutsheets.

where: Request → RECAP section. The switch-feature summary for the programming team (blocking, PIC, publish status).
example: RECAP: ALL BLOCKS, NO PIC, NON PUBLISHED
note: Recapture of switch features. Handled by P.PROG (programming), not E.FACS — but read it to understand the order. Common: NO PIC, COMPLETE/SELECTIVE block, NP (non-published), 900/COLLECT/3RD/INT'L blocks.

where: RECAP → no Preferred Interexchange Carrier (no long-distance carrier).
note: Customer has no toll/long-distance carrier. Opposite of a PIC assignment.

where: RECAP → number not listed in the directory.
note: Directory suppression. Shows as Nonpublish on the iVUE SO header.

where: RECAP → complete caller-ID blocking (number always shows PRIVATE).
note: vs Selective (SEL) where the number does appear. Caller-ID presentation control.

where: Request flag → order needs engineering/GIS design before facilities (drop placement, field meet).
note: Triggers a field meet / drawing / WO before the SO can be completed. Common on Beasore and new-area orders. Order often put in Hold.

where: Request → Assessor's Parcel Number for the property (used for vicinity maps / drop placement).
note: Parcel identifier. Looked up in ParcelQuest for EDGE/new-service inquiries and drop placement.

where: Response → field work order number for drop placement / construction.
note: Construction/field WO referenced in the response when a drop or plant work is dispatched.
